title: Attachment, the self and social development
summary: Attachment theory and research, development of the self, peer influence and the role of childhood experiences.

keyterms.definition: A strong, lasting emotional bond between an infant and a caregiver.
Ainsworth's standardized observation that classifies infant attachment by reactions to separation and reunion.
The infant is distressed when the caregiver leaves, easily comforted on return, and uses them as a safe base.
The infant shows little distress at separation and avoids the caregiver on return.
The infant is very distressed at separation and both seeks and resists comfort on return.
Bowlby: a mental template of relationships based on the early attachment.
Recognising oneself, e.g. in a mirror; usually appears between about 18 and 24 months.
The effect of same-age others on attitudes and behaviour, especially strong in adolescence.
Lack of adequate care, stimulation or attachment in early childhood.

questions.prompt: Harlow (1958) gave infant rhesus monkeys a wire "mother" with milk and a cloth "mother" without. They:
options: Spent most time with the wire mother
Spent most time with the cloth mother
Only visited the wire mother when frightened
questions.explanation: Contact comfort mattered more than food, challenging learning explanations of attachment.

questions.prompt: In the Strange Situation, which behaviour indicates insecure-avoidant attachment?
options: Intense distress and anger on reunion
Little distress on separation and avoidance on reunion
Using the mother as a safe base
questions.explanation: Avoidant infants seem independent and avoid contact with the caregiver.

questions.statement: Van IJzendoorn and Kroonenberg (1988) found secure attachment was the most common type across the countries they studied.
questions.explanation: Their meta-analysis also found more variation within cultures than between them.

questions.statement: Bowlby argued that the first attachment provides an internal working model for later relationships.
questions.explanation: The internal working model is a template for expectations of others.

questions.text: Ainsworth's standardized procedure for classifying attachment is the Strange ___.
questions.explanation: It uses episodes of separation from and reunion with the caregiver.

questions.text: Infants who both seek and resist comfort on reunion show insecure-___ attachment.
questions.explanation: Also called ambivalent attachment.

questions.prompt: Match each attachment type to reunion behaviour.
questions.explanation: Main and Solomon (1990) later added the disorganized type.

questions.prompt: Why might the Strange Situation be culturally biased?
options: It was developed with US infants, and behaviours like independence are valued differently across cultures
It was only used in Japan
questions.explanation: Higher avoidant rates in Germany and resistant rates in Japan may reflect childrearing norms, not insecurity.

questions.prompt: A key ethical problem with Harlow's research is that:
options: Infant monkeys suffered lasting social and emotional harm
questions.explanation: Today the 3Rs would demand strong justification; findings may also not generalize to humans.

questions.prompt: Order the main episodes of the Strange Situation (simplified).
items: Caregiver and infant enter the room
questions.explanation: Further separations and reunions follow; reunion behaviour is key to classification.

questions.prompt: In the rouge test (Amsterdam, 1972), most children first touched the mark on their own nose at about:
questions.explanation: Self-recognition typically emerges in the second year.

questions.prompt: Gardner and Steinberg (2005) had participants play a driving game alone or with peers watching. Peer presence:
options: Increased risk-taking most in adolescents and young adults
questions.explanation: This suggests peer influence on risky decisions is greatest in adolescence.

questions.statement: Rutter et al. found Romanian orphans adopted into UK families before 6 months showed good catch-up in development.
questions.explanation: Those adopted later were more likely to show lasting difficulties, suggesting timing of deprivation matters.

questions.statement: Erikson proposed that adolescence involves a crisis of identity versus role confusion.
questions.explanation: Erikson's psychosocial theory is a stage theory of the development of self.

questions.text: Recognising one's own reflection in a mirror is called self-___.
questions.explanation: It is an early sign of a developing self-concept.

questions.text: A lack of adequate care and stimulation in early childhood is called early ___.
questions.explanation: Rutter's study of Romanian orphans examined its effects.

questions.prompt: Match each study to its finding.

pairs.right: Early adoption helps recovery from deprivation

questions.explanation: Each shows a different influence on development.

questions.prompt: Why is Rutter's study of Romanian orphans a natural experiment?
options: Researchers randomly assigned children to orphanages
The IV (age at adoption) occurred naturally
It took place in a lab
questions.explanation: It would be unethical to manipulate deprivation; this limits control of other variables.

questions.prompt: Gardner and Steinberg's driving game may lack:
options: Ecological validity, since a game is not real driving
questions.explanation: Real-life risks and consequences were absent.

questions.prompt: Order Erikson's first four psychosocial stages.
questions.explanation: Identity vs role confusion follows in adolescence.
